summary.title: Practical Advice for New Software Engineers
summary.one_liner: Learn practical habits for new engineers, such as seeking early feedback, building end-to-end first, automating tedious tasks, and taking detailed notes.
takeaways: Get feedback early on prototypes, using a trivial PR, mockups, or sketches before writing lots of code.
Build the system end-to-end with mocked pieces first so you can see how components fit together.
Avoid premature abstraction: copy and paste while prototyping, but clean up the code before it rots.
Automate repetitive tasks, since automation also helps you actually get tasks done, not only save time.
Keep daily notes, step away from the screen to think, stay physically active, and plan the next day's to-do list.
summary.summary: This short blog post from HubSpot software engineer Ernie Park collects practical tips for engineers early in their careers. Each section gives one habit or hack with a brief personal example, such as prototyping with copy-paste before abstracting, or setting up a mocked end-to-end path before tackling the hard calculation. Other tips cover talking through problems with a colleague as a "rubber ducky," stepping away from the keyboard, automating repetitive work, keeping detailed notes, and planning the next day. The tone is informal and experience-based rather than a formal tutorial.
